modes.cue_notes: Sit with one leg in front at roughly a 90-degree angle (external rotation, shin parallel to the front of the mat) and the other leg behind at a 90-degree angle (internal rotation, shin extending behind). Sit between both legs. The front hip is in external rotation; the back hip is in internal rotation. The torso can be upright, hinge over the front shin, or rotate toward the back leg. Hold each side.

source: Traditional yin yoga; see Paul Grilley, Bernie Clark, Sarah Powers
notes: Uniquely targets both hip external rotation (front leg) and hip internal rotation (back leg) simultaneously. Liver and gallbladder meridians run the inner and outer aspects of the hip and thigh.
